pattern.crimePattern: embezzler surprised by a night guard while removing records
pattern.notes: Composite of office-block thefts; fictional building and company.

ob.text: Cleaner Nancy Akinyi reports that the night askari of Kilele House, Moi Avenue, Francis Mutua (52), was found at the foot of the 4th-floor stairwell at 06:35. Pronounced dead at the scene. The building's front door was locked from inside.

people.name: Francis Mutua
people.bio: Guarded Kilele House for eleven years. Locked the front door at 19:00 every night and walked every floor with his torch.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 50s, grey-flecked moustache, navy security guard uniform with a company badge, a heavy black torch clipped to his belt, calm proud face, ID-photo framing

people.name: Rehema Salim
people.bio: Has kept Bidii Freight's books for six years. An outside audit of the cash accounts is due on Monday.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, early 40s, patterned headscarf, neat office blouse, a laptop bag strap across her shoulder, composed but tired eyes, ID-photo framing

people.name: Isaac Kiprotich
people.bio: Repainting the 4th-floor corridor this week. Overalls spattered in Ivory Cream.

image.brief: Kenyan man, early 30s, white painter's overalls spattered with cream paint, a paint roller over his shoulder, cheerful but worried, ID-photo framing

people.name: Collins Wekesa
people.bio: Covers the day shift. Argued with Francis last week about swapping weekend shifts.

image.brief: Kenyan man, late 20s, navy security guard uniform, cap under his arm, young and defensive, ID-photo framing

people.name: Nancy Akinyi
people.bio: Starts at 06:30 every weekday. Found Francis.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, mid 40s, a blue cleaner's overall coat, hair tied back under a blue scarf, yellow rubber gloves tucked into the pocket, shaken and pale, ID-photo framing

people.name: Ali Hussein
people.occupation: Night askari, the building next door
people.bio: Guards the bank-hall building next to Kilele House. Sits by the window facing Kilele's front door and stairwell.

image.brief: Kenyan man, about 60, grey stubble, a heavy navy security greatcoat with plain buttons, a knitted black cap, a torch held at his chest, tired heavy-lidded eyes, ID-photo framing

people.name: Joyce Wekesa
people.bio: Speaks to Amani by phone from Kayole.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, mid 20s, long braids tied up, a lilac knitted sweater, small gold stud earrings, worried and a little defensive, ID-photo framing

people.name: Pastor Daniel Kioko
people.bio: Runs Tuesday-night choir practice. Speaks to Amani by phone.

image.brief: Kenyan man, late 50s, greying hair and moustache, a dark suit jacket over a pale blue shirt, reading glasses hanging on a cord, patient and courteous, ID-photo framing

places.name: Guard post, the building next door

locations.name: Kilele House, Moi Avenue
locations.description: A six-storey 1970s office block. Ground-floor desk with the visitor register. The 4th-floor corridor is half repainted: drop cloths, a ladder, tins. The stairwell window faces the building next door. A side fire door opens onto a service lane.

hotspots.label: Foot of the 4th-floor stairs
hotspots.text: Francis lies on the landing below the 4th floor. His torch is broken beside him. On his right sleeve: a smear of cream paint.

hotspots.label: Ground-floor desk: visitor register
hotspots.text: A thick ruled book. After 19:00, the night askari writes in everyone who enters and signs them out.

hotspots.label: Paint tins on the 4th floor
hotspots.text: Three tins of 'Ivory Cream' emulsion, one open. A painter's note is taped to the lid.

hotspots.label: Drop cloth in the corridor
hotspots.text: The drop cloth runs the length of the corridor. Near the stairwell door, a single shoe print has set in the paint.

hotspots.label: Side fire door
hotspots.text: The fire door onto the service lane is unlatched. Nancy says it is always latched at night.

image.brief: a dim 1970s Nairobi office stairwell at night, cream paint drying on half the corridor wall, drop cloths on the floor, a step ladder, a stairwell window looking onto the lit window of the building next door, no people

locations.name: Bidii Freight office, 4th floor
locations.description: Two desks, a filing cabinet, a calendar from a shipping line. A note on the board: 'AUDIT — Monday 9am — all cash ledgers.'

hotspots.label: Office bin
hotspots.text: Nancy empties this bin every morning. Today it holds a pair of women's court shoes wrapped in a carrier bag.

hotspots.label: Ledger shelf
hotspots.text: A row of cash ledgers, numbered by year. This year's is missing.

image.brief: a small cramped freight-agency office on the 4th floor of an old Nairobi office block at dawn, two worn desks with old computers and stacks of delivery books, a grey steel shelf of thick cash ledgers on the right with a gap in the row, a metal office bin beside the nearest desk, a window onto city rooftops, fluorescent tube light, no people
a broken black security torch lying on a concrete stair landing, a cream paint smear on the step beside it, police tape across the stairwell rail, no body visible

body.note: Final coat 4th flr corridor done 16:50. DON'T WALK. — Isaac

image.brief: an open tin of cream-coloured emulsion paint standing on a paint-spattered drop cloth in a corridor, a wet brush laid across the lid, a folded handwritten note taped to the side of the tin

body.label: Narrow heel, pointed toe, about size 38. A women's court shoe.

image.brief: a single women's court-shoe print, narrow heel and pointed toe, set in cream paint on a canvas drop cloth, with a police scale ruler beside it

body.label: Black court shoes, size 38. Cream paint on one heel.

image.brief: a pair of black women's court shoes in a crumpled carrier bag in an office bin, one heel smeared with cream paint

body.label: Cash ledgers 2019–last year. This year's: missing. Board note: AUDIT Monday.

facts.text: Francis Mutua was found at the foot of the 4th-floor stairs of Kilele House at 06:35.
The front door of Kilele House was locked from inside when the cleaner arrived.
Francis was struck or shoved, then fell down the stairs. His torch broke.
A smear of cream paint is on Francis's sleeve.
Register: I. Kiprotich, painter, signed in 08:00 and out 17:10.
Register after lock-up: R. Salim, Bidii Freight, in at 20:40. No sign-out.
After the 19:00 lock-up, the register has only one entry: R. Salim.
Register: N. Akinyi, cleaner, in at 06:30.
The paint is 'touch dry' only 4–6 hours after it goes on.
Painter Isaac Kiprotich put the final coat on the corridor at 16:50.
A size-38 women's court-shoe print set in the wet paint by the stairwell door.
Size-38 court shoes with cream paint on one heel are in the Bidii Freight office bin.
This year's Bidii Freight cash ledger is missing from its shelf.
An audit of all Bidii Freight cash ledgers is set for Monday at 9.
Ali saw only one person enter Kilele House after 19:00: a woman with a laptop bag, at about 20:40.
At about 21:15 Ali saw a torch moving in Kilele's 4th-floor stairwell window and heard a shout.
Ali's own guard book shows him at his post all night, 19:00 to 06:00.
The side fire door was unlatched when Nancy arrived. It is always latched at night.
Nancy says Mzee Ali next door watches Kilele's door all night from his window.
Nancy says the day askari, Collins Wekesa, argued with Francis last week about weekend shifts.
Nancy was at home in Mathare North until she left for work at 05:50.
Joyce: Collins was home in Kayole all evening. The neighbours' kesha kept everyone awake past midnight.
Pastor Kioko: Isaac sang at choir practice in Kariobangi from 19:30 to 21:45, then helped stack chairs.
Isaac: "I signed out at ten past five and went to choir."
Collins: "I was home in Kayole. I didn't like Francis, but I didn't come back here."
Rehema: "I came back for some files and left. I didn't see anyone."
Rehema says she wears flat shoes home and leaves her office shoes in the office.
Isaac warned everyone on the 4th floor that the corridor would be wet until late night.

interrogations.intro: Nancy has her mop in both hands like a staff. "Eleven years he greeted me every morning. Every morning."

topics.reply: Francis did his rounds every hour with that big torch. Every floor. He was proud of that torch.
I clean Bidii Freight first, every morning. The bin is always just paper. Today there were shoes in it. Shoes!
Collins and Francis shouted at each other last week about weekend shifts. Young men shout.
Mzee Ali next door sits at his window all night. Nothing happens on this street he doesn't see.

interrogations.intro: Ali speaks slowly, choosing every word. "I keep a book too. Askari to askari, we watch each other's doors."

topics.reply: A woman with a laptop bag, about twenty to nine. Francis let her in and wrote in his book. I didn't see her come out of the front.
The painter? He left before dark, at five or so. Singing.

interrogations.intro: Isaac keeps wiping his hands on his overalls though they're dry. "I told everyone. Don't walk on my corridor."

topics.reply: Final coat at ten to five. That paint stays tacky till nine, ten at night. I told the whole floor.
That's not my boot. My boots are size 44. And I walk on the cloth edges, like a professional.
Call Pastor Kioko. Tuesday is choir. I've never missed a Tuesday.

interrogations.intro: Collins arrives for his day shift and stops dead at the tape. "Francis? Kwani what happened?"

topics.reply: We argued about Saturdays. He wanted me to cover. I said no. It was nothing. Call my wife.

interrogations.intro: Rehema answers the door of her flat in Parklands already dressed for work. "Kilele House? I was there last night, yes. Briefly."

topics.reply: I keep a pair of office shoes in the office and go home in flats. Doesn't everyone?
The audit is routine. Every year. I don't see what that has to do with Francis.

chargeSheet.template: {who} caused the death of {victim} at Kilele House.

prosecutor.pass: One entry after lock-up, one shoe in the paint, the same shoe in her bin. It will hold.
fail: This doesn't hold up. Who was actually inside that building after seven?
No. The paint tells you when. The register tells you who. Read them together.

proof.concludes: The print was made in wet paint, after 16:50 and before late night, by someone in a size-38 women's court shoe.
The only person inside Kilele House after lock-up was Rehema Salim, and her office shoes carry the cream paint.

eliminations.why: Isaac signed out at 17:10 and was at choir practice in Kariobangi from 19:30 to 21:50.
Collins was home in Kayole, kept awake by the neighbours' kesha, and nobody but the woman with the laptop bag entered after 19:00.
Nancy only arrived at 06:30, long after the 21:15 shout.
Ali's guard book places him at his own post next door all night.

reconstruction.text: Monday's audit will show the cash Rehema has been skimming from Bidii Freight. On Tuesday night she comes back for this year's ledger.
20:40. Francis unlocks the front door for her and writes her in. He doesn't think twice: she's worked upstairs for six years.
About 21:15. Ledger in her bag, Rehema crosses the wet corridor in her office shoes. Francis's torch finds her at the stairwell door. He asks what she's carrying.
She shoves him. He falls. She changes into her flats, drops the painted shoes in her own office bin, and leaves by the side fire door.
The painter, covered in Ivory Cream, was singing in Kariobangi the whole time.

tier1.line: Every office block in Nairobi keeps a book at the front desk. Read it like a list of suspects.

tier2.line: A shoe print in the paint, and a pair of shoes in a bin. Whose bin?

glossary.def: All-night prayer vigil, usually with loud singing.
Respectful word for an older man.
"But why…?" or "So what…?": a word of surprise or protest.

ui.beatNotes: Found paper: the visitor register opens as a full-screen ruled book the player scrolls; facts lift out of it line by line. First time window in the notebook: Ali's 21:15 shout gets a clock icon.
